source.title: The Andre-Oort conjecture for A_g
readSections: All twelve published PDF pages inspected as screenshots

summary: André-Oort for A_g through discriminant-orbit and CM lift-height bounds. This continuation makes the quadratic-Hecke deduction of the CM height bound explicit at the imported-theorem level, identifies the existing discriminant tower theorem, and assigns quantitative extensions without duplicating the general CM, height or analytic foundations. The four mixed-Shimura items are routed to LD.6 as a source-scoped André–Oort endpoint; recursive primary-proof checks of cited sources remain prerequisite work.

items.name: CM fields
items.statement: A number field E is CM when it is a totally imaginary quadratic extension of a totally real field E0. Write [E:Q]=2g and [E0:Q]=g; E need not be Galois over Q.
items.note: Directly checked at the mathlib pin in CMField.lean, blob 6c7067617742aae433a648031822e84a41746b4f, lines 63-91. The class uses the maximal real subfield and assumes Field and CharZero. No Lean elaboration was run.
api: maximalRealSubfield and its degree
complex conjugation and fixed elements
totally complex infinite-place pairs
unitTests: Q(i) has maximal real field Q and degree two.
A real quadratic field fails IsCMField.
A non-Galois quartic CM field is allowed; no IsGalois assumption is introduced.

items.name: CM types
items.statement: A CM type Phi is a set of embeddings E -> C choosing exactly one embedding from each conjugate pair. The type of an O_E-action on a dimension-g abelian variety is its tangent-space representation.
api: finite embedding set with disjoint conjugate complement
tangent representation of the specified O_E-action
transport under CM field isomorphism and complex conjugation
unitTests: An imaginary quadratic field has two singleton types.
Selecting both members of one conjugate pair fails the type axiom.
Different types on the same quartic field stay distinct before a proved equivalence.

items.name: Primitive CM types
items.statement: A CM type is primitive when it is not induced from a CM type on a proper CM subfield by restriction of embeddings.
api: induced type by restriction from a CM subfield
primitive predicate with its explicit proper-subfield quantifier
simple maximal-CM endomorphism theorem as a consumer
unitTests: Every imaginary quadratic type is primitive.
An induced type from an imaginary quadratic subfield of a biquadratic CM field fails primitivity.
A non-Galois CM field with no proper CM subfield has primitive types; Galoisness is not required.

items.name: The CM class set S(E,Phi)
items.statement: S(E,Phi) consists of O_E-equivariant isomorphism classes of dimension-g complex abelian varieties with injective O_E-action of tangent type Phi. This is not a set of principally polarized isomorphism classes.
api: objects with injective O_E-action and tangent type
equivariant isomorphism relation and quotient
ideal-class action and choice-independent class-number comparison
unitTests: For an imaginary quadratic maximal order the unpolarized equivariant class set has h_E elements.
Adding a chosen principal polarization changes the moduli problem and requires a separate comparison.
Twisting the specified action can change tangent type even when the underlying abelian variety is unchanged.

items.name: Polarized field of moduli
items.statement: For a polarized abelian variety over Qbar, its field of moduli is the fixed field of the stabilizer of its polarized isomorphism class, equivalently the residue field of the coarse moduli point. A model over that field is not part of the definition.
items.locator: 1, p. 379 and footnote p. 380; Lemma 4.1, p. 384
items.note: M6 explicitly separates rational coarse moduli points, objects over a field, and the descent obstruction. The numerical extension-degree estimate below is an additional theorem, not automatic from a coarse point.
api: Galois stabilizer of polarized isomorphism class
fixed field and coarse residue-field comparison
field-of-definition map and descent obstruction
unitTests: A model over k gives a stabilizer containing Gal(Qbar/k).
The carrier does not return a k-model merely from a k-rational coarse point.
For elliptic curves over Qbar the coarse field is Q(j), regardless of the field of one chosen equation.

items.name: Hodge determinant with its metric
items.statement: For A/K with everywhere semistable reduction, construct the determinant of invariant differentials of its Neron model over O_K and its archimedean metric from integration of omega wedge conjugate(omega). Import the Neron model and determinant-line foundations.
api: determinant of invariant differentials on semistable Neron model
finite lattice and archimedean norm
base change, tensor and section-scaling maps
unitTests: Replacing a section by a nonzero scalar changes each norm by its absolute value.
The zero section is excluded from the finite-index height formula.
Scaling the squared metric by (2*pi)^(-g) leaves the finite lattice unchanged.

items.name: Stable Faltings height
items.statement: For the Hodge line L and nonzero omega, set h_F(A)=(log #(H0(L)/O_K omega) -(1/2) sum_sigma log |integral sigma(omega wedge conjugate(omega))|)/[K:Q], after a field extension giving everywhere semistable reduction.
api: normalized arithmetic degree
semistable extension and extension-independent value
product and metric-scaling comparisons
unitTests: A further finite semistable base extension leaves the normalized height unchanged.
Product-formula cancellation removes a scalar change of nonzero section.
Negative height values are admitted; Bost is a real lower bound.

items.name: Independence of the Hodge section
items.statement: Replacing the nonzero Hodge section leaves the height unchanged: the product formula cancels the finite-index and archimedean changes.

items.name: Stable height under field extension
items.statement: The normalized height after semistable reduction is unchanged by further finite extension, so it is independent of the chosen semistable field. Existence of semistable reduction is an imported theorem, not automatic for the initial model.

items.name: Bost lower bound
items.statement: For each g there is a real c_g with h_F(A)>=c_g for every dimension-g abelian variety over Qbar; the source records linear dependence on g. The lower bound need not be positive.

items.name: CM ideal-class classification
items.statement: S(E,Phi) is nonempty and has cardinality h_E=#Cl(E), through the lattice/ideal-class classification. This counts equivariant unpolarized classes, not principally polarized CM points.

items.name: Bounded-degree Brauer-Siegel
items.statement: For number fields of bounded degree and discriminant D tending to infinity, log(h_K R_K)=(1/2+o(1)) log D. Keep fixed-degree uniformity and possible ineffectivity explicit.
items.note: EffectiveBounds' long-term aspiration is not an established implementation of this input.

items.name: Discriminant tower for a CM field
items.statement: For a tower of number fields F subset E, D_E=N_(E/Q)(different(O_E/O_F))*D_F^[E:F]. For a CM extension [E:F]=2 this gives D_E=D_F^2*N_(E/Q)(different(O_E/O_F))>=D_F^2. The norm of the relative discriminant is the same integer as this absolute norm of the relative different.
items.note: The general tower identity is read at the mathlib pin in NumberField/Discriminant/Different.lean:89-99, with integral-closure/finiteness/scalar-tower hypotheses. Specialize to rings of integers and the quadratic maximal-real subfield. This is an import of the existing different-norm identity; no new relative-discriminant carrier or Lean elaboration is claimed.

items.name: CM regulator comparison
items.statement: For arbitrary CM E, R_E/R_E0=2^(Units.rank E)/indexRealUnits(E), where indexRealUnits(E) is 1 or 2. Thus the ratio is bounded in terms of g for [E:Q]=2g.
items.note: Directly checked in pinned CMField.lean, blob 6c7067617742aae433a648031822e84a41746b4f, lines 365-445. No IsGalois Q E hypothesis is needed. This corrects the earlier working note; do not re-plan the regulator comparison.

items.name: CM relative class-number growth
items.statement: For fixed g and epsilon>0, h_E/h_E0>=C_{g,epsilon}|Disc(E)|^(1/4-epsilon) for CM E of degree 2g and sufficiently large discriminant, with a small-discriminant adjustment if required.

items.name: Endomorphisms for primitive maximal CM
items.statement: For primitive Phi and A in S(E,Phi), End_C(A)=O_E with the specified action; isogenies between objects of this fixed-type class set respect that action. Retain primitivity and the maximal order.

items.name: Isogeny attached to an ideal
items.statement: For nonzero integral I in O_E and A with O_E-action, form the common kernel T_I of the endomorphisms in I and the quotient A -> A/T_I. Construct equivariance, preservation of CM type, and descent of the finite subgroup scheme.
api: finite subgroup annihilated by a nonzero ideal
quotient abelian variety with descended O_E-action
kernel, norm-degree, composition and base-field descent
unitTests: The unit ideal gives the trivial kernel and identity isogeny.
For the principal integer ideal (m), the degree is m^(2g) when m is nonzero.
The zero ideal is excluded: it would annihilate no endomorphism beyond zero and give the whole variety as kernel.

items.name: Ideal-isogeny classification and degree
items.statement: Under primitive maximal CM, nonzero integral ideals classify the relevant target-and-isogeny pairs from fixed A; the degree of A -> A/T_I is N(I), and all classes in S(E,Phi) are mutually isogenous.

items.name: Uniform bounded-norm ideal count
items.statement: For degree 2g fixed and epsilon>0, the number of integral ideals of norm n is O_{g,epsilon}(n^epsilon), so the number of norm <=X is O_{g,epsilon}(X^(1+epsilon)). Constants are uniform in E.
items.note: Do not replace this by the pinned quadratic estimate in small-ideal-count-quadratic-library. The n^epsilon coefficient estimate and its constants must be uniform over fields of fixed degree; a fixed-field asymptotic is not sufficient.

items.name: Distant CM isogenies
items.statement: For primitive Phi, there are A,B in S(E,Phi) whose minimum complex isogeny degree is >=C_{g,epsilon}|Disc(E)|^(1/4-epsilon). The preceding proof fixes A arbitrarily and yields the stronger interface: for every A there is such a B.
items.note: The strengthened starting-point quantifier is needed to prove the moduli bound for every A.

items.name: Masser-Wustholz quantitative isogeny bound
items.statement: For each g there are positive C_g,kappa_g such that geometrically isogenous dimension-g A,B defined over a common number field k admit a complex isogeny of degree <=C_g max(1,h_F(A),[k:Q])^kappa_g. No polarization preservation is imposed.
items.locator: Theorem 2.3, p. 383; [12], Theorem II and field-degree discussion
items.note: [12] printed pp. 7 and 24 were inspected. Remove polarization-degree dependence using Zarhin's trick. R28.4's qualitative isogeny theorem is not this estimate.

items.name: Height constancy for a CM type
items.statement: All members of S(E,Phi) have the same stable Faltings height, denoted h_F(E,Phi).

items.name: Colmez character coefficients and conductors
items.statement: For a CM field's normal closure and a CM type, construct the rational coefficients c_{rho,Phi} and Artin conductors f_rho in Colmez's expression, fixing representations, conjugation and normalization conventions.
items.note: The individual Colmez conjecture is not a proved input.
api: normal-closure group and conjugacy-averaged type function
irreducible-character coefficients and Artin conductor
finite combinatorial bounds and averaged expression
unitTests: The trivial factor is isolated before evaluating at s=1.
Changing to the conjugate type preserves the applicable averaged identity.
The individual conjectural formula is not a theorem constructor; only the imported averaged formula is proved input.

items.name: Averaged Colmez formula
items.statement: Sum over all 2^g CM types: sum_Phi h_F(E,Phi)=sum_Phi sum_rho c_{rho,Phi}(L'(0,rho)/L(0,rho)+(1/2)log f_rho), with the representations and conventions of the published formula.
items.note: Reuse paper jobs #1143 and #1145, including the latter's 2023 erratum, rather than duplicating their deep proofs. The published conductor coefficient is one half.

items.name: Uniform character data in fixed dimension
items.statement: For fixed g, possible normal-closure groups, representation dimensions and Colmez coefficient sizes lie in a bounded finite-combinatorial family. Split off the trivial Artin factor as a dimension-dependent constant before evaluating other factors at 1.
items.note: The trivial factor has a pole at 1; do not apply the nontrivial-factor estimates to it. Original Artin-route obligation retained for source fidelity. The verified quadratic-Hecke deduction of the height bound does not assert this stronger general-Artin interface proved.

items.name: Sufficient conductor-discriminant estimate
items.statement: For representations occurring in the fixed-degree Colmez expression, establish log f_rho<=C_g(1+log |Disc(E)|). This is sufficient to absorb the conductor term in |Disc(E)|^epsilon.
items.note: This is a sufficient contract awaiting verification, not an unchecked assertion of the source's literal f_rho<=|Disc(E)|. Original Artin-route obligation retained for source fidelity. The verified quadratic-Hecke deduction of the height bound does not assert this stronger general-Artin interface proved.

items.name: Logarithmic functional equation
items.statement: For the relevant nontrivial Artin factors with nonzero L(0,rho), the completed functional equation relates L'/L(0,rho) to L'/L(1,conjugate(rho)), a conductor logarithm and fixed-degree archimedean terms. Track conjugation and gamma factors.
items.note: AN.4 explicitly includes completed Hecke/Dedekind/Artin interfaces and meromorphic continuation distinguished from Artin holomorphy. General Hecke functional equations are supplied through AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.1. This placement does not verify the uniform value/derivative estimates or license a Cauchy argument for arbitrary Artin functions.

items.name: Two-sided subpolynomial values at one
items.statement: For the relevant nontrivial Artin factors, prove two-sided subpolynomial control of the nonzero values at 1 using Brauer induction and bounded-degree Hecke/Brauer-Siegel inputs, allowing ineffective constants.
items.note: Brauer pole cancellation and trivial-character factors need explicit handling; an upper bound alone does not bound the reciprocal. Original Artin-route obligation retained for source fidelity. The verified quadratic-Hecke deduction of the height bound does not assert this stronger general-Artin interface proved.

items.name: Derivative estimate for the height proof
items.statement: Establish |L'(1,conjugate(rho))|<=C_{g,epsilon}|Disc(E)|^epsilon for the relevant factors, or a direct logarithmic-derivative bound sufficient for Corollary 3.3.
items.note: The source sketches Cauchy plus convexity. Justify the contour or work at the Hecke/averaged-expression level without assuming Artin holomorphy; this interface remains open in the extraction. Original Artin-route obligation retained for source fidelity. The verified quadratic-Hecke deduction of the height bound does not assert this stronger general-Artin interface proved.

items.name: Subpolynomial CM height
items.statement: For every g and epsilon>0 there is C_{g,epsilon}>0 with h_F(A)<=C_{g,epsilon}|Disc(E)|^epsilon for primitive maximal-CM A in S(E,Phi), uniformly in E,Phi,A.
items.note: A complete deduction from the displayed imported contracts is now given through the quadratic-Hecke nodes. General Artin Cauchy estimates are retained as original-proof obligations but are no longer prerequisites of this consumer. Recursive proofs of Brauer-Siegel, Rademacher convexity, conductor-discriminant, Bost and averaged Colmez remain imported source work.

items.name: Level-three rigidification and descent
items.statement: From a polarized A with field of moduli F, adjoin the third roots of unity and full level-3 data to rigidify the moduli problem and construct a model over an extension of degree bounded solely in g.
api: full ordered 3-torsion data and rigidification
Galois stabilizer of level data and effective descent
roots of unity, dual torsion and field-degree bound
unitTests: Retaining mu_3 makes the dual 3-torsion rational through the Weil pairing.
A residual automorphism must act trivially on full level 3 before descent is invoked.
Replacing 3 by 2 cannot reuse the rigidity theorem: the [-1] automorphism acts trivially on 2-torsion.

items.name: Definition of endomorphisms and polarizations
items.statement: Let A,B be abelian varieties over F and n>=3 prime to char(F). Every geometric homomorphism A->B is defined over any extension containing all n-torsion of both A and B. In characteristic zero apply n=3 to End(A), and to Hom(A,A^vee) after adjoining mu_3 and using the Weil pairing.
items.note: The exact sufficient theorem is explicitly stated and attributed to Silverberg 1992 in the introduction of Silverberg-Zarhin, Rigidity theorems for abelian varieties (author PDF). This corroborates the hypotheses without claiming that original Proposition 2.3 was read. Descent of a polarization morphism is not automatically descent of a chosen ample line bundle.

items.name: Bounded field of definition
items.statement: For polarized dimension-g A with field of moduli F, there is F'/F of degree <=2*3^(4g^2) defining A, all its endomorphisms and all its polarizations.
items.note: This published lemma is absent from arXiv v5.

items.name: Common small field for the CM pair
items.statement: Descend the ideal quotient B=A/T_I over F_A' using its defined endomorphisms. The published construction F_A'F_B' defines both A,B and has degree over F_A bounded by 4*3^(8g^2).
items.note: Check polarization conventions on the quotient. Do not apply the isogeny estimate over an unrealized coarse field of moduli.

items.name: Primitive maximal-CM moduli-degree bound
items.statement: For each g>=1 there are delta_g,c_g>0 such that polarized dimension-g A with primitive O_E-CM and End(A)=O_E satisfies [Q(A):Q]>=c_g |Disc(E)|^delta_g.

items.name: Centre order of a CM point
items.statement: For CM x in A_g, define R_x=Z(End(A_x)) and its integral trace-form discriminant. Allow nonsimple abelian varieties and nonmaximal orders; do not replace this by one maximal CM field.
api: centre of the actual integral endomorphism ring
embedding as full order in a product of CM fields
trace pairing, discriminant and finite-index comparison
unitTests: For a simple maximal-CM variety the centre order is O_E.
For a product of distinct simple factors use a product order, not a NumberField instance.
Replacing O by an index-f suborder multiplies the absolute discriminant by f^2.

items.name: Reflex field and type
items.statement: For primitive (K,Phi), use the normal closure L and the stabilizer of the extended type to construct the reflex field K* and reflex type Phi*, with explicit embedding and coset conventions.
api: normal closure and extended embedding set
stabilizer fixed field and induced reflex embeddings
change of normal closure and primitive double reflex comparison
unitTests: The imaginary quadratic reflex field is the original field.
A non-Galois quartic type may have a different reflex field, so do not identify carriers.
Changing the normal closure by a compatible embedding transports the reflex data rather than altering its isomorphism class.

items.name: Reflex norm on ideals and elements
items.statement: Construct t:I_{K*}->I_K by the product of conjugate extended ideals prescribed by the reflex type; construct the corresponding element norm t' and prove compatibility on principal ideals.
api: reflex norm on ideals with declared admissible domain
element norm and principal-ideal compatibility
idele/ideal and conjugation dictionaries
unitTests: A principal ideal maps to the ideal of its element reflex norm.
The unit ideal maps to the unit ideal.
The scalar norm of an ideal of K-star is N_(K-star/Q), never the ill-typed N_(K/Q).

items.name: Reflex class-group maps
items.statement: Descend the reflex norm to r:Cl(K*)->Cl(K), and form r_tilde=r composed with N_{L/K*}:Cl(L)->Cl(K). The two domains are distinct.
api: well-defined map Cl(K-star) to Cl(K)
composition with Cl(L) to Cl(K-star) norm
image/kernel and bounded-index transport
unitTests: A principal ideal represents zero and maps to zero.
The normal-closure composite has domain Cl(L), which cannot be silently identified with Cl(K-star).
For the identity field extension the norm composite equals the original reflex class map.

items.name: Index of the normal-closure class norm
items.statement: The image of N_{L/K*}:Cl(L)->Cl(K*) has index <=[L:K*]=O_g(1). Thus a power lower bound for #im(r) passes to #im(r_tilde) up to a dimension-dependent factor.

items.name: Polarized reciprocity subgroup
items.statement: H consists of classes [I] in Cl(K*) with r(I)=(a) and a*conjugate(a)=N_{K*/Q}(I), using fractional-ideal normalization. Prove independence of the representative and H<=ker(r).
items.note: The ideal norm must have the reflex-field domain; the printed subscript is incompatible with I.
api: fractional-ideal/principal-generator condition
representative independence and subgroup proof
map to positive real units modulo CM norms
unitTests: The identity ideal with a=1 lies in H.
Changing a principal generator by a unit changes the obstruction by its CM norm.
Being in ker(r) without a trivial positive-unit obstruction does not certify membership in H.

items.name: Positive-unit obstruction
items.statement: The map from ker(r) given by a*conjugate(a)/N_{K*/Q}(I) lands in O_{K0}^{times,+}/N_{K/K0}(O_K^times), has kernel H, and gives [ker(r):H]<=2^g. Use real units squared as norms and the unit rank.

items.name: Reciprocity and moduli degree
items.statement: With the reflex base field and polarized stabilizer explicit, CM reciprocity gives the sufficient inequality [Q(A):Q]<=C_g[Cl(K*):H]<=C_g*2^g*#im(r).
items.note: Check the exact equality/base-field conventions directly; absolute moduli degree and reflex-field-compositum degree cannot be conflated.

items.name: Reduction to primitive reciprocity images
items.statement: Fix g. Suppose that for every h<=g, normal-closure reciprocity images for all primitive degree-2h CM types have positive-power lower bounds in the field discriminant, with constants depending only on h (and the permitted epsilon). Then there are c_g,delta_g>0 such that every CM point x of A_g has absolute Galois orbit at least c_g*abs(disc Z(End(A_x)))^delta_g.
items.locator: Published section 5, p. 386; Tsimerman 2012, arXiv:1103.5619, Theorem 7.1 and sections 7.1-7.2, PDF pp. 17-22
items.note: The hypothesis is needed in EVERY smaller simple dimension, not just dimension g. The source reduction is now read: it combines class-group norm projections with a compact-index bound for the nonmaximal centre order. Detailed local proof leaves and published-version notation reconciliation remain.

items.name: Orbit bound for arbitrary CM points
items.statement: For each g there exist b_g,C_g>0 such that |Disc(R_x)|<=C_g |Gal(Qbar/Q).x|^b_g for every CM point x in A_g(Qbar).

items.name: Siegel uniformization and fundamental set
items.statement: Form H_g from symmetric complex matrices with positive definite imaginary part and pi:H_g->A_g(C) for Sp_(2g)(Z). Construct the fundamental-set setup and finite boundary multiplicities used in counting.
items.note: Do not assert a globally free coarse covering or that an open fundamental domain includes its boundary.
api: symmetric matrix carrier with positive definite imaginary part
symplectic action and coarse moduli uniformization
selected fundamental set, boundary multiplicities and height adapter
unitTests: For g=1 the carrier reduces to the upper half-plane.
A symmetric matrix with a zero imaginary eigenvalue is excluded.
Points with nontrivial stabilizer retain orbifold isotropy; the coarse map is not assumed a free covering.

items.name: Special and weakly special subvarieties
items.statement: Use Shimura data and the fixed-factor description to define special and weakly special subvarieties and their lifts. A weakly special fixed factor may be nonspecial; the notions are distinct.
items.note: Import Shimura-data foundations from their owner; LD.6 owns the functional-transcendence interface.
api: Shimura-subdatum special locus
fixed-factor weakly special locus and lifts
CM-point promotion, dimension and Galois transport
unitTests: A positive-dimensional factor at a nonspecial fixed parameter is weakly special without being special.
A weakly special subvariety containing a CM point is promoted by the separate theorem.
A zero-dimensional special subvariety is a special point, not every complex point.

items.name: Reduction to algebraic coefficients
items.statement: For algebraic V over C, pass to components of the Qbar-defined Zariski closure of its CM points and choose number fields of definition. The dense-CM assertion there yields the finite-maximal-special formulation using Noetherianity.

items.name: Height and degree for algebraic lifts
items.statement: Use absolute multiplicative Weil height on algebraic coordinates and maximum height on coordinate tuples. Fix the coordinatewise algebraic degree bound before counting; transport heights under finite field extension and between complex entries and real-imaginary coordinates by named comparisons.
items.note: RP.0 supplies absolute heights and field-extension compatibility. The specific Siegel-coordinate comparison belongs to the CM lift theorem, not to a second height definition in LD.6.
api: absolute multiplicative coordinate height
coordinatewise degree and tuple maximum
extension invariance and complex-to-real coordinate bounds
unitTests: Rational a/b in lowest terms has height max(abs(a),abs(b)).
Field extension leaves the absolute height unchanged.
Several individually quadratic coordinates can generate a field of degree greater than two; coordinatewise and joint degree are different APIs.

items.name: Bounded degree of CM lifts
items.statement: For fixed g there is a degree bound d_g for the algebraic coordinates of CM representatives in the selected Siegel fundamental set, independent of the centre-order discriminant. The counting theorem must use this same coordinatewise degree convention, including the conversion to real and imaginary coordinates.
items.locator: Published section 6.2; Pila-Tsimerman 2013 section 3, PDF pp. 5-9; Pila-Tsimerman 2014 Lemma 7.4
items.note: The inspected 2013 arXiv text says at most 4g for entries in its simple-case construction; the 2014 text uses 2g. This checkpoint retains only a dimension-dependent bound, does not identify it with joint coordinate-field degree, and leaves the numerical/convention reconciliation explicit.

items.name: Polynomial CM lift-height bound
items.statement: Suitable representatives y of a CM point x satisfy H(y)<=C_g|Disc(R_x)|^a_g, for constants depending only on g and with the exact height/degree conventions of the cited theorem.
items.note: The complete proof of the all-dimensional Theorem 3.1 in arXiv:1106.4023 section 3 was read. It includes nonmaximal-order lattice reduction, bounded Riemann forms and symplectic bases, quantitative Siegel reduction, and an isotypic reduction. Some printed intermediate expressions use the maximal-order discriminant where the order index also enters; preserve the final dependence on disc(R) and reconcile with the published edition before formalising those intermediate statements.

items.name: O-minimality of R_an,exp
items.statement: The real field with restricted analytic functions and exponentiation is o-minimal, with definable-set closure and cell-decomposition APIs.

items.name: Definable restricted uniformization
items.statement: Restricted Siegel uniformization on the chosen fundamental set is definable in R_an,exp, so its inverse image of algebraic V intersected with that set is definable.

items.name: Algebraic part of a definable set
items.statement: T_alg is the union of connected positive-dimensional semialgebraic subsets of T, in the Pila-Wilkie convention; it is not the Zariski closure of T.
api: union of connected positive-dimensional semialgebraic subsets
membership witness and containment in the original definable set
counting complement without assuming the algebraic part definable
unitTests: A finite definable set has empty algebraic part.
A real interval is entirely in its algebraic part.
The graph of restricted exponential on an interval has no semialgebraic arc despite its positive-dimensional Zariski closure.

items.name: Bounded-degree Pila-Wilkie
items.statement: For definable T, a fixed algebraic degree bound d and epsilon>0, the number of degree-<=d points of height <=X in T outside T_alg is O_{T,d,epsilon}(X^epsilon). Include the extension from rational points.

items.name: Orbit growth gives many bounded-height lifts
items.statement: For V defined over F, the Gal(Qbar/F)-orbit of a CM point in V has at least its absolute orbit size divided by [F:Q]. Discriminant invariance, lift-height bounds and finite multiplicities then give a power lower bound for the algebraic-point count in the definable preimage.

items.name: Northcott for lift coordinates
items.statement: Bounded degree and bounded height give finitely many algebraic coordinate tuples, so infinitely many distinct CM points force unbounded counting parameters.
items.note: Accepted AUDIT-09 distinguishes existing fixed-number-field element Northcott from the needed bounded-degree algebraic-point theorem. RP.0 explicitly imports/plans the latter and its absolute-height compatibility; do not rebuild it in LD.6.

items.name: From semialgebraic pieces to complex algebraic pieces
items.statement: A maximal connected irreducible semialgebraic subset of a complex analytic set, in the sense of [16], is a complex algebraic subset to which Ax-Lindemann can apply.
items.note: An arbitrary real semialgebraic arc is not itself the needed complex algebraic variety.

items.name: Hyperbolic Ax-Lindemann for A_g
items.statement: For algebraic V in A_g, each maximal irreducible complex algebraic subset of pi^{-1}(V) is weakly special in the precise lifted sense.
items.note: The conclusion is weakly special, not automatically special.

items.name: A CM point promotes weakly special to special
items.statement: A weakly special subvariety of A_g containing a CM point is special, by the fixed-factor Shimura description.

items.name: Finiteness of CM points avoiding positive-dimensional special loci
items.statement: For fixed V, all but finitely many CM points lie on positive-dimensional special subvarieties contained in V, by the orbit/height bound, bounded-degree counting, algebraicity of maximal pieces and Ax-Lindemann.

items.name: Finite reduction of the weakly special locus
items.statement: For an algebraic V in A_g, its positive-dimensional weakly special locus is a countable union of closed algebraic subvarieties and is definable in R_an,exp. The source finite-union lemma and the maximal-orbit construction then reduce the relevant CM-containing families to finitely many semisimple Q-subgroup types, with their normalizer and maximality conditions retained.
items.locator: Published section 6.5, p. 388; Pila-Tsimerman 2014 section 7, Lemmas 7.5-7.7 and final argument, pp. 677-678
items.note: Correction: Lemma 7.2 on p. 674 proves normalizer reductivity; it is NOT the finite-family theorem. Compactness restrictions are on rational factors in the source, not a blanket ban on compact real factors.

items.name: Induction through weakly special families
items.statement: For each fixed subgroup F, if N(F)_sh is proper in the generic Mumford-Tate group, use finitely many proper special envelopes and lower-dimensional intersections with V. If N(F)_sh is the whole group, pass through the finite product map to the closed whole-fibre parameter locus, whose dimension is smaller; maximal fibres correspond to isolated special parameters. Combine induction with the finite reduction of families and bounded-discriminant exceptional-point finiteness.
items.locator: Published section 6.5, p. 388; Pila-Tsimerman 2014 Theorem 7.1 proof, pp. 674-678
items.note: The full final argument has now been read. Two different dimension drops must be implemented; the previous one-line induction item did not expose them.

items.name: Andre-Oort for A_g
items.statement: For every g>=1, every irreducible closed algebraic V in A_g contains only finitely many maximal special subvarieties; equivalently, an irreducible subvariety with Zariski-dense CM points is special.
items.note: The scope is A_g in all dimensions, not all Shimura varieties.

items.name: The stated mixed-Shimura consequence
items.statement: For a mixed Shimura variety whose pure part is a Shimura subvariety of A_g, the paper records Andre-Oort: every irreducible subvariety with dense special points is special. Apply Gao Theorem 13.6 after supplying Tsimerman's pure Galois-orbit bound; the dimension restriction in Gao's earlier unconditional corollary is thereby removed in this stated scope.
items.locator: Published introduction, p. 380; Gao section 13, Theorems 13.3 and 13.6, Remark 13.5
items.note: The section-13 reduction and proof have now been read. This consequence uses the pure ORBIT bound, not merely the already-proved pure Andre-Oort conclusion. Full mixed foundational ownership and earlier Gao theorem proofs remain to be extracted; no claim for all mixed Shimura varieties is made.

items.name: Existing quadratic bounded-norm ideal estimate
items.statement: For every number field F and real X>=1, the set of nonzero integral ideals I of O_F with absNorm(I)<=X is finite, and its cardinality is at most X^2*2^[F:Q].
items.note: Direct signature and namespace read at f790474. Auxiliary weaker input, not the near-linear estimate printed in Proposition 2.2; using it changes the intermediate exponent.

items.name: Existing real-side analytic class-number formula
items.statement: For a number field K, as real s tends to 1 from above, (s-1)*dedekindZeta(K,s) tends to the positive real number 2^r1*(2*pi)^r2*R_K*h_K/(w_K*sqrt(abs(discr K))).
items.note: Directly read at 082e2d3. This is a right-real limit for the existing L-series. Complex meromorphic continuation and functional equations are NOT supplied by these declarations; neither is Brauer-Siegel uniformity.

items.name: Dual level-three torsion from the Weil pairing
items.statement: In characteristic zero the perfect Weil pairing identifies A^vee[3] with Hom(A[3],mu_3). Therefore rationality of all A[3] and mu_3 over a field implies rationality of all A^vee[3] over that field.
items.locator: Published Lemma 4.1 proof; Silverberg-Zarhin introduction; abelian-scheme Weil pairing
items.note: This uses the pairing with the dual, not an unjustified principal polarization of an arbitrary ideal quotient. Keep roots of unity and the prime-to-characteristic condition.

items.name: CM isotypic decomposition with multiplicities
items.statement: For a dimension-g complex CM abelian variety choose an isogeny to a product of powers A_i^n_i of pairwise nonisogenous simple CM abelian varieties, with sum n_i*dim(A_i)=g. Write K_i=End^0(A_i); these fields may be isomorphic for inequivalent CM types. The centre of End^0(A) is the product of K_i, while End^0(A) is the product of M_(n_i)(K_i).
items.locator: Tsimerman 2012 section 7.1; Pila-Tsimerman 2013 section 3, general case
items.note: Import Poincare complete reducibility and semisimple End from AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A6 and the primitive CM classification from V5. Matrix sizes are multiplicities n_i, not dimensions g_i.
api: isogeny to pairwise nonisogenous simple factors with multiplicities
endomorphism-algebra block comparison
centre product and dimension identity
unitTests: For A=B^n the block is M_n(End^0(B)), not M_dim(B).
Different nonisogenous factors may have isomorphic CM fields without being merged into one isotypic block.
The dimension check sums multiplicity times simple-factor dimension.

items.name: Discriminant of the CM centre order
items.statement: With R=Z(End(A)) inside O=product O_(K_i), R is a full Z-order and abs(disc R)=[O:R]^2*product abs(disc K_i).
items.locator: Tsimerman 2012 section 7.2; Pila-Tsimerman 2013 section 3, general case
items.note: The square is the ORDER index. It is not literally the square of the Mumford-Tate compact-subgroup index; the latter is compared by a separate inequality. General product orders go beyond a single NumberFieldOrder carrier. The arXiv notation in the 2012 reduction needs reconciliation against the published version.

items.name: CM compact-subgroup index controls the centre order
items.statement: For a CM point x of fixed dimension g, let T=MT_x, K_x=T(A_f) intersect GSp_(2g)(Zhat), and T(Zhat) the maximal compact subgroup. With O=product O_(K_i) and R=Z(End(A_x)), there are positive constants c_g,d_g such that [O:R] <= [T(Zhat):K_x]^c_g * (product abs(disc K_i))^d_g, in the notation and integral realization of the source.
items.note: Proof inputs are generation by Mumford-Tate/reflex-trace elements, local lattice indices, sufficiently convergent p-adic exponentials, and a Vandermonde/Nakayama argument. Do not identify the two indices or omit ramified primes. At p=2 the exponential depth must be increased.

items.name: Bounded bases for CM lattices
items.statement: For a degree-2g CM field K and a full Z-lattice I contained in O_K, there is a Z-basis of I all of whose conjugates are bounded by a polynomial in abs(disc K)*[O_K:I], with constants depending only on g. For a lattice with multiplier order R, first scale it into O_K with index polynomial in abs(disc R).
items.note: Use the actual real covolume 2^(-g)*sqrt(abs(disc K))*[O_K:I] for the standard complex embedding, not a literal unsquared discriminant covolume. This corrects a compressed printed expression without changing polynomial dependence.

items.name: Quantitative reduction to a Siegel fundamental set
items.statement: Fix g and Z=X+iY in H_g with Y positive definite. Put h(Z)=max(max_ij abs(z_ij),1/det(Y)). In the source reduction, symplectic integral changes sending Z to the chosen standard fundamental set have coordinates polynomially bounded in h(Z); combine this with algebraic-height transformation bounds to control the reduced CM representative.
items.note: This is stronger than existence of a fundamental set and requires the specified normalization. Keep a separate proof that bounded entries/conjugates/denominators yield absolute Weil-height bounds.

items.name: Reductivity of the connected normalizer
items.statement: In the source section-7 setup, for a connected semisimple Q-subgroup F of the generic Mumford-Tate group G arising from a maximal weakly special orbit, the connected normalizer N_G(F)^0 is reductive.
items.note: An intermediate algebraic-group lemma. The application consumes it; a final blueprint must import any general reductive-normalizer API rather than construct it again here.

items.name: Finitely many special envelopes for a fixed subgroup
items.statement: Fix F in the source set C of connected semisimple Q-subgroups of G with no compact Q-factors and admitting a weakly special orbit. Let N(F) be its connected normalizer, Com(N(F)) the product of the compact Q-factors of N(F)^ad, and N(F)_sh=ker(N(F)->Com(N(F)))^0. The set of special subvarieties of H_g of the form N(F)_sh(R)^+ y with y(S) contained in N(F)_sh,R is finite as y varies over H_g.
items.locator: Pila-Tsimerman 2014, definition after Lemma 7.2 and Lemma 7.3, pp. 674-675
items.note: Do not replace this by finiteness of all weakly special translates: such translates can vary continuously. The condition on the Deligne torus and the source ambient/lifted locus are essential.

items.name: Countable algebraic decomposition of the weakly special locus
items.statement: For an algebraic V contained in A_g, the union of its positive-dimensional weakly special subvarieties is a countable union of closed algebraic subvarieties of V.
items.note: Use countably many rational Shimura subdata and factorizations, and the algebraic locus where a whole positive-dimensional factor lies in V. Do not infer finiteness from countability alone.

items.name: Definability of the weakly special locus
items.statement: For algebraic V in A_g, the union of its positive-dimensional weakly special subvarieties is definable in R_an,exp in the canonical definable structure.
items.note: The proof needs the finiteness of real semisimple embedding types up to conjugacy, definable dimension/maximality, and restricted uniformization; it is not closure of definable sets under arbitrary countable unions.

items.name: A definable countable algebraic union is a finite subunion
items.statement: Let A be a complex quasiprojective variety and (V_i) a countable family of closed complex algebraic subvarieties. If the union of the V_i is definable in R_an,exp, then it equals the union of finitely many of the V_i.
items.note: Use finite real-analytic cell decomposition, a Baire/dimension argument giving a full-dimensional intersection, and analytic continuation. This is not a theorem for arbitrary countable families of definable subsets, nor is an arbitrary o-minimal analytic-cell theorem assumed.

items.name: The algebraic parameter locus for whole special fibres
items.statement: In the fixed-family proof, if N(F)_sh=G, then F is normal and the almost-direct product with its centralizer gives a finite Shimura product map. Form the closed algebraic locus V_prime in the complementary factor consisting of parameters whose entire F-factor fibre is contained in the inverse image of V. In the positive-dimensional F case, dim(V_prime)<dim(V).
items.note: The condition is containment of the WHOLE fibre, not merely nonempty intersection. Keep the finite cover and descent to the original V explicit.
api: finite Shimura product cover in the normal-factor case
algebraic locus of parameters whose whole fibre lies in V
dimension bound and special parameter to larger special locus map
unitTests: If V contains a whole positive-dimensional factor fibre, its parameter belongs to the locus.
A parameter with only a single intersection point in its fibre does not qualify.
A positive-dimensional special parameter family gives a special locus strictly larger than one maximal fibre.

items.name: Maximal special fibres have isolated special parameters
items.statement: In the normal-factor parameter locus above, a special parameter lying on a positive-dimensional special subvariety produces a strictly larger special subvariety containing the corresponding F-fibre. Thus maximal special F-fibres are controlled by isolated special points of the lower-dimensional parameter locus, to which induction applies.
items.note: This is the missing induction bridge between pointwise special coverage and finite maximality.

items.name: Transport special subvarieties back from a conjugate point
items.statement: Let V be defined over a number field k. If sigma in Gal(Qbar/k) sends a special point x of V into a positive-dimensional special subvariety S contained in V, then sigma^(-1)(S) is a positive-dimensional special subvariety of V containing x.
items.locator: Pila-Tsimerman 2014, proof of Lemma 7.4, p. 676; canonical-model Galois compatibility
items.note: The counting argument can find a conjugate, not the originally chosen x. Canonical-model stability of special subvarieties and V/k are necessary.

items.name: Unipotent denominator of a mixed special point
items.statement: Fix the mixed datum, a Levi decomposition P=W semidirect G, integral lattices and the neat level specified in Gao section 13. For a special point represented by a conjugate wTw^(-1) with w in W(Q), let N(s) be the positive integral denominator ord(w) in the source coordinates.
items.note: It agrees with torsion order in a semiabelian fibre only up to the stated fixed constants. It is not a coordinate-free order on every mixed Shimura variety without those choices.
api: fixed Levi decomposition and integral coordinates
denominator of w in W(Q)
level-change comparison and pure projection compatibility
unitTests: For w=identity the denominator is one.
In the Kuga torsion-fibre case compare with torsion order only using the source constants.
Changing lattice or level requires a comparison theorem; the numerical denominator is not declared invariant.

items.name: Mixed orbit growth from the pure orbit and denominator
items.statement: For the fixed mixed datum and level of Gao section 13, reflex field E, projection pi to the pure part, and 0<epsilon<1, there exists C_epsilon>0 independent of the special point s such that |Gal(Qbar/E)s| >= C_epsilon*N(s)^(1-epsilon)*|Gal(Qbar/E)pi(s)|.
items.note: The proof separately controls the compact-torus index, Euler factors and B^(number of prime divisors). No GRH is used for this relative mixed-to-pure inequality. The base reflex field and fixed level are retained.

items.name: Conditional mixed Andre-Oort in the source scope
items.statement: Let S be a connected mixed Shimura variety of abelian type in Gao Theorem 13.6, and Y a closed irreducible subvariety with Zariski-dense special points. If the specified positive-power pure special-point orbit bound (13.8) holds for the pure part, then Y is special.
items.locator: Gao, arXiv:1310.1302, Theorem 13.6 and proof, PDF pp. 49-50
items.note: Imports mixed Ax-Lindemann (Theorem 1.2), the quotient/dimension reduction of Theorem 12.2, definability and bounded-degree counting, not pure Ax-Lindemann with the word mixed substituted. Only section 13 was read in full in this continuation.

items.name: Quadratic Hecke character of a CM extension
items.statement: For a quadratic CM extension E/F with F totally real of degree g, obtain the nontrivial order-two idele-class character eta_E/F through global reciprocity. At every real place its component is sign; its primitive finite conductor is distinguished from an arbitrarily larger ray modulus. Use the existing field/idele character supplier.
items.locator: Yuan-Zhang, published p. 535, Theorem 1.1; Thorner-Zaman 2017, pp. 1140-1141
api: idele-class character and primitive finite conductor
sign component at every real place
Euler-factor values and completed-function comparison
unitTests: For E=Q(i), F=Q, recover the odd quadratic Dirichlet character of conductor 4.
At a ramified prime omit the primitive local factor; at split and inert primes its values are 1 and -1.
Enlarging a ray modulus must not enlarge the primitive conductor or silently delete additional Euler factors.

items.name: Conductor of the quadratic CM character
items.statement: The finite conductor of eta_E/F is the relative discriminant ideal. Consequently the finite analytic conductor Q=D_F*N_(F/Q)(f_eta)=D_E/D_F lies in [1,D_E]. Do not identify Q with D_E unless F=Q.
items.locator: Yuan-Zhang Theorem 1.1; quadratic conductor-discriminant comparison needed by the application
items.note: Standard quadratic class-field-theoretic comparison is an explicit imported proof leaf; its original proof was not read in this continuation.

items.name: Quadratic zeta factorization and the residue quotient
items.statement: For Re(s)>1, zeta_E(s)=zeta_F(s)*L_f(s,eta_E/F), including ramified Euler factors. By the positive simple-pole residues and holomorphy of the nontrivial Hecke L-function at 1, L_f(1,eta)=kappa_E/kappa_F>0. Use an analytic continuation adapter before interpreting the real-side library residue as a complex residue.
items.locator: Quadratic Euler-factor calculation; Thorner-Zaman 2017 equations (2-1)-(2-7); main Corollary 3.3 adapter

items.name: Entire nontrivial quadratic Hecke L-function
items.statement: For the primitive nontrivial quadratic character eta_E/F, L_f(s,eta) is entire; its completion is entire of order one. The statement excludes the trivial character and retains all primitive Euler factors.
items.locator: Thorner-Zaman 2017 p. 1141, equations (2-3)-(2-7); AL.1 Tate continuation

items.name: Completed functional equation with totally odd infinity type
items.statement: Put Gamma_R(s)=pi^(-s/2)*Gamma(s/2). For eta_E/F, Lambda(s)=Q^(s/2)*Gamma_R(s+1)^g*L_f(s,eta) satisfies Lambda(s)=w*Lambda(1-s) with constant |w|=1. Here eta is real and each real place is odd. No trivial-character s(s-1) factor occurs.

items.name: Uniform subpolynomial Dedekind residues
items.statement: For every n>=1 and epsilon>0 there are c,C>0 depending only on n,epsilon such that c*D_K^(-epsilon)<=kappa_K<=C*D_K^epsilon for every number field of degree at most n. Constants may be ineffective. Derive from bounded-degree Brauer-Siegel, the explicit residue formula, the bounded number of roots of unity, and a finite adjustment for small discriminants. Normality is not added to the bounded-degree contract.
items.locator: Brauer 1947 input as used in main sections 2-3; Tsimerman arXiv:1103.5619v3 Lemma 4.1 for comparison
items.note: The original Brauer 1947 proof was not obtained; this is a precise remaining source leaf. Tsimerman 2012 Lemma 4.1 is a stronger corroborating tori statement, not a substitute claim that its induction proof is fully decomposed.

items.name: Two-sided quadratic Hecke value bound
items.statement: For every fixed g and epsilon>0, D_E^(-epsilon) <<_(g,epsilon) L_f(1,eta_E/F) <<_(g,epsilon) D_E^epsilon. Constants may be ineffective. Use kappa_E/kappa_F, the degree bounds 2g and g, and D_F<=D_E^(1/2), choosing each residue exponent at most 2*epsilon/3.

items.name: Uniform finite-order Hecke convexity
items.statement: Let chi be a primitive finite-order Hecke character over a degree-n number field K, Q=D_K*N(f_chi), 0<r<=1/2, and -r<=sigma<=1+r. For s=sigma+it, |L_f(s,chi)| << |(1+s)/(1-s)|^delta(chi) * zeta_Q(1+r)^n * (Q*(3+|t|)^n/(2*pi)^n)^((1+r-sigma)/2), with an absolute implied constant. The pole factor is present only for the trivial character; zeta_Q means the Riemann zeta function.
items.locator: Thorner-Zaman 2017, Lemma 2.3, printed p. 1142; credits Rademacher 1959
items.note: The statement and its variable-field constant convention on p. 1140 were read; the displayed formula was checked visually. Rademacher original proof remains a prerequisite. This is a uniform statement, not a fixed-K convexity estimate.

items.name: A fixed small circle gives a subpolynomial derivative
items.statement: For fixed g and every epsilon>0, |L_f prime(1,eta_E/F)| <<_(g,epsilon) D_E^epsilon. Set r=min(epsilon,1/4)>0. The closed circle |s-1|=r is in [-r,1+r] in real part, |t|<=r, and the convexity exponent is at most r. Hence its supremum is at most C_(g,r)*Q^r, and Cauchy gives |L_f prime(1)|<=C_(g,r)*Q^r/r. Holomorphy is required on the entire disk; a zero-free disk is unnecessary.
items.locator: Derived from Thorner-Zaman Lemma 2.3 and Cauchy derivative estimate

items.name: Subpolynomial logarithmic derivative at one
items.statement: For every fixed g and epsilon>0, |L_f prime(1,eta)/L_f(1,eta)| <<_(g,epsilon) D_E^epsilon. Apply the derivative bound with epsilon/2 and the reciprocal value bound with epsilon/2. The latter, rather than Cauchy, is the possible ineffective input.

items.name: Logarithmic functional equation at zero and one
items.statement: For ell_j=L_f prime(j,eta)/L_f(j,eta), both denominators are nonzero and ell_0+ell_1=-log Q+g*(gamma+log(2*pi)), where gamma is Euler constant. Differentiate the completed functional equation; Gamma_R prime/Gamma_R at 1 and 2 sum to -gamma-log(2*pi). Nonvanishing at 0 follows from the functional equation and L_f(1)>0.
items.locator: Derived from Thorner-Zaman (2-3)-(2-6), odd gamma factors

items.name: Comparison of the two printed height conventions
items.statement: Let h_T use Tsimerman p. 381 and h_YZ use Yuan-Zhang p. 534, on the same semistable model. Their finite determinant lattices coincide, whereas ||omega||_YZ^2=(2*pi)^(-g)*||omega||_T^2. With the degree-weighted archimedean sum, h_YZ=h_T+(g/2)*log(2*pi).
items.locator: Tsimerman published p. 381; Yuan-Zhang published p. 534, both images checked
items.note: Derived comparison, not a quotation of a common normalization. Rescaling the norm downward increases the arithmetic degree. The additive constant is harmless for the height bound but must precede substitution of the exact average formula.

items.name: Averaged Colmez in quadratic Hecke normalization
items.statement: For all 2^g CM types of a degree-2g CM field E with maximal real field F and eta=eta_E/F, 2^(-g)*sum_Phi h_YZ(E,Phi)=-(1/2)*L_f prime(0,eta)/L_f(0,eta)-(1/4)*log Q, with Q=D_F*N(f_eta)=D_E/D_F. The sum includes imprimitive types.
items.note: Import the theorem with its metric through existing issue #1145 (Yuan-Zhang) and its 2023 erratum, or reconcile issue #1143 (AGHMP). Do not duplicate the 106-page averaged-Colmez proof in this application roadmap.

items.name: From a quadratic Hecke average to each CM height
items.statement: The preceding formula and gamma comparison give avg(h_T)=(1/4)*log Q+(1/2)*ell_1-(g/2)*gamma-g*log(2*pi). Consequently |avg(h_T)| <<_(g,epsilon) D_E^epsilon. Since all 2^g heights are >=c_g, every h_T(E,Phi)<=2^g*avg(h_T)-(2^g-1)*c_g <<_(g,epsilon) D_E^epsilon. The real lower constant c_g need not be positive, and primitivity is unnecessary for this height step.
items.locator: Derived proof of main Corollary 3.3 using the quadratic average

items.name: Uniform coefficient bound by a divisor function
items.statement: For a degree-n number field K, n>=1, let a_K(m) count nonzero integral ideals of norm m. For every m>=1, a_K(m)<=d_n(m), where d_n counts ordered n-tuples of positive integers with product m. At each rational prime the Euler factor product over p-adic prime ideals (1-T^f_i)^(-1) is coefficientwise bounded by (1-T)^(-n), since f_i>=1 and the number of factors is <=n; multiply over primes.
items.locator: Elementary decomposition of the ideal-count input in main section 2.2
items.note: This proof uses unique ideal factorization and residue degrees, not the numerical quadratic count. The library item supplies compatible ideal/norm carriers only; the coefficient theorem itself is not claimed in the pinned library.

items.name: Subpolynomial fixed-order divisor function
items.statement: For each integer n>=1 and epsilon>0 there is C_(n,epsilon) with d_n(m)<=C_(n,epsilon)*m^epsilon for every m>=1. Use d_n(p^a)=binomial(a+n-1,n-1). For large p this is <=n^a<=p^(epsilon*a); for the finitely many smaller primes the supremum of the polynomial in a divided by p^(epsilon*a) is finite. The product of those finitely many constants is independent of m.
items.locator: Elementary fixed-degree proof of the bound used in main section 2.2

items.name: Explicit exponent choice in the primitive orbit argument
items.statement: If the distant-isogeny lower bound holds with every exponent a<1/4, the height has every positive subpolynomial exponent, and the Masser-Wustholz exponent is kappa_g>0, then every 0<delta<1/(4*kappa_g) is admissible in [Q(A):Q]>>_(g,delta)D_E^delta. Choose delta*kappa_g<a<1/4 and height exponent epsilon<a/kappa_g. After absorbing dimension constants, N>>D_E^a forces the common field degree term in the isogeny maximum for all sufficiently large D_E; its bounded ratio to the moduli degree gives the assertion. Adjust the positive constant for the finitely many smaller integral discriminants.
items.locator: Main Theorem 4.2 proof, explicit quantifier/constant adapter

Import the averaged Colmez theorem through the dedicated #1143/#1145 paper routes, including the Yuan-Zhang erratum; construct the normalization/application adapter here rather than duplicate those deep proofs. Target exactly: for every g>=1, primitive maximal-CM polarized dimension-g A has [Q(A):Q]>=c_g*D_E^delta_g for dimension-dependent c_g,delta_g>0; every CM point x in A_g satisfies abs(disc Z(End(A_x)))<=C_g*|Gal(Qbar/Q).x|^b_g; and its chosen Siegel fundamental-set lift has coordinatewise degree bounded in g and height <=C_g*abs(disc Z(End(A_x)))^a_g. Primitive-to-general reduction requires every simple dimension h<=g, product centres with repeated isomorphic fields, nonmaximal orders, the square of the order index, and a separate compact-index comparison including p=2. For lift height, retain lattice covolume/order index, Riemann forms, symplectic bases, quantitative Siegel reduction and complex-to-real coordinate height/degree adapters. Source edition and reciprocity-stabilizer gaps in this partial intake are mandatory acquisition/verification tasks before executable blueprints.
